title: Suggestion Enforcer: gated rollout and canary policy for Optimize recommendations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a 'Suggestion Enforcer' component that can safely auto-apply Optimize batching/caching recommendations with a gated rollout and explicit canary policies. The goal is to capture ~10-25% token-cost savings on compatible workloads while ensuring no regressions in latency, error rate, or quality. This ticket implements the server-side orchestration, enforcement rules, and operator-facing controls necessary to: (1) stage recommendations into cohorts, (2) progressively shift traffic using traffic shaping and feature flags, (3) validate metrics against guardrails, and (4) require human approvals at defined escalation points. The implementation must integrate with existing Optimize suggestion engine, Console rollout UI, and the tracing/observability pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Can stage a recommendation to a named cohort (dev, beta, production) via API and Console
Traffic can be routed by percent to cohort variants with a minimum granularity of 1%
Automated checks evaluate latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, token throughput, and quality regressions within 10-minute windows
If any guardrail trips (see monitoring_checks), the enforcer stops rollout, pauses traffic shift, and notifies on-call and the owning PM/Engineer
Manual approval flow available in Console to continue past a pause with audit log entry
Playable rollback that reverts config within 2 minutes of trigger and emits an incident event to PagerDuty and Slack channel #optimize-rollouts
E2E tests and synthetic canary jobs included in CI that simulate 3 traffic cohorts and validate policy behavior
Documentation (Confluence + Console tooltips) published and linked from PR
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Canary tests in CI using synthetic traffic (low risk) - done by engineer
Stage 1: Internal dev orgs (<=5% traffic) for 24h - check cost delta and latency
Stage 2: Beta customers (segmented by label) (5-25% traffic) for 48h - run quality evals on sample prompts
Stage 3: Production ramp in pulses (25->50->100) with operator approval at 50% if any non-critical warnings
Stage 4: Post-rollout monitoring for 7 days with daily regression reports and cost realization dashboard
monitoring_checks: Latency regressions: P99 increase > 5% vs baseline => pause rollout
Error rate: 5xx increase > 2x baseline or absolute 0.5% => immediate rollback
Throughput: token-per-second drop > 10% for production pool => alert
Cost delta: expected token cost reduction within +/- 15% of predicted; divergence > 15% => investigate
Quality: automated eval set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop > threshold (model-specific) => hold
Anomaly detection: spike in retry/queueing metrics or scheduler backpressure => pause
rollback_strategy: Automatic rollback: enforcer maintains last-known-good configs and prioritized revert actions. On trigger, shift 100% traffic back to baseline within 120s and create a revert PR that documents the cause. If automatic rollback fails, escalate to on-call and require manual operator revert. Post-rollback, run a postmortem checklist (metrics snapshot, top-k requests, correlation with PRs), and create follow-up ENG tickets for root cause.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from noisy metrics leading to unnecessary pauses. Mitigation: use smoothed baselines (10-minute rolling medians) and require sustained deviation for two consecutive windows before auto-rollback.
Risk: Customer-facing latency spikes. Mitigation: start in low-impact cohorts and enforce per-org circuit breakers
Risk: Quality regressions undetected by automated evals. Mitigation: sample human-in-the-loop review for first 1000 production responses and add targeted prompt sets
Risk: Race between optimizer apply and other config deploys. Mitigation: acquire cluster-level apply lock and surface conflicts in Console
implementation_notes: Add new 'enforcer' table in Optimize control plane to track recommendation state, cohorts, and applied configs (schema doc linked in PR)
Extend routing layer to accept cohort tags and percentage-based weights; reuse existing feature-flag infra for traffic shaping
Expose an operator API to pause/resume/pin a recommendation and to force-revert
Integrate with tracing: tag requests with recommendation_id and cohort for correlation in Jaeger and Grafana
Unit and integration tests must mock scheduler/backpressure events and validate rollback timing
